title: India Just Walked Into the Cannes of Animation. 'Baahubali: The Eternal War' Is Maahishmati's Most Daring Bet Yet.
excerpt: SS Rajamouli's animated saga has been picked for the Work in Progress lineup at Annecy 2026 — the world's most prestigious animation stage. Prabhas is back as Baahubali's soul, this time fighting a cosmic war across 14 realms.
body:
The last image we have of **Amarendra Baahubali** is a betrayal — Kattappa's blade, the slow disbelief, a kingdom's golden son falling. For nearly a decade that was the end of the story everyone wept over. But **SS Rajamouli** was never going to let that soul rest. What if the prince didn't simply die? What if his spirit crossed into the afterlife and walked straight into a war older than Maahishmati itself?

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=iDqSKfIQ-q4</youtube>

That is the audacious premise of **Baahubali: The Eternal War**, and this month it did something no Baahubali film has done before: it went to France. The two-part animated saga has been officially selected for the **Work in Progress** showcase at the **Annecy International Animation Film Festival 2026**, the event so revered in the medium that it's universally nicknamed the "Cannes of animation." The festival ran June 21 to 27, which means right now, as you read this, top international critics are getting their first proper look at what Indian animation can do at full scale.



> **"It is a rare honor for Indian mainstream cinema that Baahubali: The Eternal War has been selected for the Work in Progress lineup at Annecy 2026." — SS Rajamouli

Let that selection sink in."**


> "I have always believed animation offers a canvas with no boundaries. It is a rare honor for Indian mainstream cinema that Baahubali: The Eternal War has been selected for the Work in Progress lineup at Annecy 2026." — SS Rajamouli

Let that selection sink in. India's biggest live-action franchise — a brand that redefined the scale and ambition of pan-Indian cinema — is now planting a flag in the one arena where Indian films have historically been guests, not headliners. Annecy's Work in Progress sessions invite filmmakers to pull back the curtain mid-production, walking audiences through the artistic process. For a country whose animation industry has long been treated as outsourced labor for Hollywood, having an original Indian IP invited to that table is a genuine inflection point.

The story is pure mythological fever dream. Following his death in the mortal world, **Amarendra Baahubali** — voiced once again by **Prabhas** — finds himself drawn into an ancient cosmic battle between the **devas and asuras**, spanning 14 mystical realms of existence. He forges unlikely alliances, confronts divine forces beyond mortal comprehension, and fights to restore balance to the cosmos. **Ramya Krishnan** returns to voice **Sivagami**, the matriarch whose presence anchored the original films. Rajamouli has been emphatic that this is **not Baahubali 3** — it's a full-length animated universe expansion, a new journey told through a wholly different medium.

The creative pedigree is what makes this more than a vanity spin-off. The film is directed by **Ishan Shukla**, an acclaimed indie animator who helmed an episode of *Star Wars: Visions* and the festival-feted feature *Schirkoa: In Lies We Trust*. He's working with a richly detailed 3D animation style benchmarked against global standards. Rajamouli and **Shobu Yarlagadda** — the producing duo behind the original duology — reunite as co-producers alongside Prasad Devineni, and the score comes from Oscar-winner **MM Keeravani**, whose 'Naatu Naatu' already proved Indian film music could conquer the Dolby Theatre.

Backed by **Arka Media Works** with a reported budget of around ₹120 crore, *The Eternal War* is one of the most ambitious animated films India has ever attempted. Part 1 is targeting a late-2027 theatrical release. Rajamouli, who has fallen hard for anime in recent years — he's spoken openly about his love of *Demon Slayer* and *Attack on Titan*, and is even exploring an anime version of *RRR* with Japanese studios — called the *Eternal War* teaser "stunning, crafted with top-tier quality and imagination worthy of Baahubali's magnificence."

The timing couldn't be sharper. Indian animation just had its breakout commercial moment with **Mahavatar Narsimha**, which stunned the trade with a worldwide haul north of ₹300 crore — proof that audiences will fill theatres for homegrown animated mythology. *The Eternal War* now carries that momentum onto a global prestige stage.

For the diaspora, this one lands differently. NRI parents have spent years trying to pass down the Ramayana and Mahabharata to kids raised on Pixar and Studio Ghibli, often losing the battle to slicker production values. A Baahubali animated epic — Indian mythology rendered at international quality, in a format their children already love — is the bridge many families have been waiting for. Annecy 2026 is the world being told it's coming. Late 2027 is when the diaspora's living rooms, and then theatres across the US, UK and Canada, finally get to see it. Jai Maahishmati, indeed.
